replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: I see mathematics as a language that describes patterns, not something I love or hate. It's a tool that helps me understand the world, especially in chemistry and physics, even if I don't always enjoy working with it.
replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Sometimes, yes. When I have to solve equations under time pressure or when I don't immediately understand a concept, I feel a tightness in my chest. But I try to breathe through it and break problems into smaller steps.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: Yes, I used an AI chatbot to check my solutions and explain steps I didn't understand. It was helpful when it gave clear explanations, but sometimes it was too technical or assumed knowledge I hadn't fully grasped yet.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write the equation in standard form. Then, factor it or use the quadratic formula: x equals negative b plus or minus the square root of b squared minus four a c, all over two a. Finally, check both solutions by plugging them back in.

Take the derivative of the function to get f'(x). Set that derivative equal to zero and solve for x. Those x-values are where the function has stationary points. Then, plug them back into the original function to find the y-coordinates.
replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: PCA reduces data dimensions by finding directions of maximum variance.
